clue.text: Used person in dock to trap Queen fan

indicators.note: to trap means one word closes around the other, holding it inside

parts.note: the person in the dock at a trial is the accused
a queen is a female cat, and a tom, the male, is her admirer

explanation.surface: A defendant in court supposedly ensnares a devoted follower of the rock band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the band or the monarch, but a queen is also a female cat, whose admirer is the male. 'to trap' puts him inside the defendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Being used to something is a common synonym for being habituated or familiar with it.

clue.text: German pal briefly accepting help up sort of slips

indicators.note: accepting means the first word takes the second into itself
briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Freund is the German word for friend

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is a synonym for help

explanation.surface: A German friend takes in some assistance and makes a revealing verbal slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the final D of the German word; 'up' reads the help word upwards before 'accepting' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freudian slip is a verbal error thought to reveal hidden desires, so the word describes a kind of slip.

clue.text: Sibyl's upset about more expensive 22D

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the other piece
upset in a down clue means the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a sibyl is a prophetess, a seer; the 's is read as 'is', a link
prices that are up are higher, more expensive

explanation.surface: A prophetess is unsettled by something costing more money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the prophet word into REES, which goes 'about' the price word. 22D refers to the answer at 22 down, CASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupees are the currency of India and Pakistan, so they are a form of money.

clue.text: Bundles of notes with bills

parts.note: bills are posters or advertisements, ads

explanation.surface: Banknotes gathered in bundles, together with invoices.
explanation.definitionFit: A wad is a thick roll or bundle, especially of banknotes.

clue.text: Warehouse salesman, old one in fiction

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: in means the letter for one sits inside the word for fiction

parts.note: a story is a piece of fiction
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A warehouse salesman appears as a former character in a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository is a place where goods are stored, essentially a storehouse.

clue.text: Southern vineyard Penny managed had reservations

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its wine
led means managed or ran

explanation.surface: Penny, running a vineyard in the south, had doubts about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' reads as a woman's name, but it is just P.
explanation.definitionFit: To scruple is to hesitate on moral grounds, so the past tense means had misgivings.

clue.text: Illicit spirit bottle regularly hidden by writer

indicators.note: hidden by means the picked letters are tucked inside the writer word

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of bottle is taken

explanation.surface: A bottle of bootleg liquor is concealed by an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'bottle'; 'writer' looks like an author but is the instrument, and 'hidden by' tucks the picked letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Poteen is Irish moonshine, traditionally distilled illegally from potatoes or grain.

clue.text: One can bend vertically

indicators.note: vertically in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: a tin is a can
a U is a U-bend, a bend shaped like that letter

explanation.surface: A single item that can flex up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is a tin; 'vertically' reads TINU from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing regarded as a whole, so it means one.

clue.text: Distribute foreign article about copper

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
foreign means the letters of article are made strange, rearranged

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Hand out an overseas newspaper piece about a policeman, or the metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign article' suggests LE or UN, but 'foreign' rearranges ARTICLE to CIRLATE, which goes about CU.
explanation.definitionFit: To circulate something is to pass it around or spread it among people.

clue.text: Start to cultivate mountain ash without a top

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of cultivate is used
without means a letter is left out of the tree name

parts.note: rowan is another name for the mountain ash tree

explanation.surface: Begin to grow a mountain ash tree whose upper part has been lopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a top' looks like a single instruction, but 'without a' drops A from ROWAN and 'top' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown is the topmost part of the head or of a tree.

clue.text: Reliable Republican probes American moneylenders

indicators.note: probes means the first pieces push inside the abbreviation for American

parts.note: US is short for American, as in the US
sure means reliable or dependable

explanation.surface: A trustworthy Republican investigates American loan sharks.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurers lend money at exorbitant interest, so they are moneylenders.

clue.text: Work fast to impress posh lush

indicators.note: to impress means pressing one piece into the middle of another

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
Lent is the Christian period of fasting
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Labour quickly to win over a smart, heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lush' looks like a drunkard, but here it means luxurious; 'to impress' presses the posh letter between the two other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush can mean luxurious and rich, which is a synonym for sumptuous wealth.

clue.text: Reverse ends

definitions.meaning: the reverse side of a coin, the side without the head
rear ends or back parts, as of animals or shirts

explanation.surface: Turn around the final parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tails is the back of a coin, and tails are hindmost ends of things.

clue.text: Tweets about rise in 22D previously

indicators.note: about means the bird-song word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a bird that tweets sings
a hill is a rise in the ground

explanation.surface: Social media posts about an earlier price increase in money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweets' looks like social media; it is birds singing. 22D is CASH, so the definition means old money.
explanation.definitionFit: Shillings were British coins until decimalisation in 1971, so they are former currency.

clue.text: In which top candidates appear lean in sportswear

indicators.note: in means the word for lean sits inside the clothing word

parts.note: shorts are worn for sport
to list is to lean, as a ship does

explanation.surface: The best applicants turn up looking slim in athletic gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortlist is the final selection of the strongest applicants for a post.

clue.text: Firm resolve to put crocodiles in small river

indicators.note: in means the crocodiles word goes inside the river name

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs, so crocodiles are lines

explanation.surface: It takes determination to release crocodiles into a little stream.
explanation.walkthrough: A British 'crocodile' is a file of children walking two by two; the Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeliness is hard, unyielding determination, the quality of firm resolve.

clue.text: Employer of donor disputed ridiculously easy profit

indicators.note: disputed means the letters are argued over and thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The employer of a donor is contested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disputed' rearranges the fifteen letters of 'Employer of donor'.
explanation.definitionFit: This British idiom means payment or gain for very little effort.

clue.text: Fancy making yen first

indicators.note: first means the yen letter comes before the other piece

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen
earning means making money

explanation.surface: Wanting to make Japanese money before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as a noun is a desire or longing, which is a synonym for strong wanting.

clue.text: Unlike a bikini formerly covering European bird

indicators.note: covering means the outer word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: once means formerly
pie is an old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: Swimwear of old covering a European bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-part swimsuit, so a single-garment swimsuit is its opposite.

clue.text: Duke quickly releases first note with reserve

indicators.note: releases first means the earlier of the two copies of a letter is let go from the word for quickly

parts.note: instantly means at once, quickly

explanation.surface: An aristocrat hastily lets go of his first message while staying aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releases' drops the first N from INSTANTLY, leaving ISTANTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting distantly means being cool and aloof, behaving with reserve.

clue.text: Ready briefcase to impress English king

indicators.note: to impress means the pieces are pressed into the shortened case word

parts.note: a case is a shell; brief shortens it by its last letter
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A briefcase at hand, ready to win over an English monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefcase' splits into 'brief' and 'case': SHELL cut short to SHEL, round EK.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready is slang for cash, and the shekel is a currency, so it is money.

clue.text: Hull market restricts hotel

indicators.note: restricts means the trading word hems in the other letter

parts.note: to market is to sell
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A market in the city of Hull limits a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' looks like the Yorkshire city, but it is the outer casing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hull is the outer covering or husk of a seed, a synonym for a casing.

clue.text: Western horse lives awfully close to river

indicators.note: awfully means the letters of lives are badly jumbled
close to means only the last letter of river is used

explanation.surface: A cowboy's horse leads a terrible life near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges LIVES to SILVE, plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver was the Lone Ranger's horse in the classic television and radio Westerns.

clue.text: Can I spread round chicken Madras earlier?

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the other piece
spread means the letters of can I are scattered into a new order

parts.note: a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: A diner asks to spread a chicken curry before the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken Madras' looks like the curry; the definition is cryptic: the city was named Madras earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city now called Chennai was officially known as Madras until 1996.

clue.text: Change Roman coin in Switzerland

indicators.note: in means the coin sits inside the country code

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
the as was a bronze coin of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: Exchange a Roman coin while in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Change means coins or money, which is a synonym for ready money.

clue.text: Backing some Arabian oil limits big figure

indicators.note: Backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Supporting some limits on Arabian oil production is a huge number.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand thousand is a large number, so it is a big figure.

clue.text: Notebooks in pristine condition

parts.note: split note-books: mi is a sol-fa note and NT, the New Testament, is books; the rest defines the whole as perfect condition

explanation.surface: Notebooks that are still in perfect condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notebooks' is one word that must be split: 'Note' is MI in sol-fa and 'books' is NT, the New Testament; 'in pristine condition' defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint describes something as new and unused, a synonym for perfect condition.

clue.text: Rick's piano? No way

indicators.note: no means the following word is removed from the piano maker's name

parts.note: a Steinway is a famous make of piano
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is this Rick's piano? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: Rick Stein is a well-known British TV chef; 'No way' looks like an exclamation but removes WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rick Stein is a British television chef, so his surname completes the name.

clue.text: Redraft sentence about piano pieces

indicators.note: about means the reworked letters go round the other piece
redraft means the letters of sentence are written out again in a new order

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Rewrite a line of text about a musical instrument's compositions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' looks like musical works; it means coins. 'Redraft' rearranges SENTENCE, around P.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenpences are former British coins worth ten pence, so they are pieces of money.
